observed_text:
Before cleaning, the general inspection material directs that the initial appearance of the bearings and the amount and condition of residual lubricant be recorded, and that the lubricant be sampled before the bearings are cleaned [EV-K01-009]. For lubricant handling, used lubricant samples from bearings, housing and seal areas should be kept separately packaged and properly labelled, and a sample of new, unused lubricant should be secured; any available specification or batch information from the container should be recorded (inclusive OR, not a requirement that both exist), and technical specifications plus any related material safety documentation should accompany lubricant shipments [EV-K01-006]. Broader preparation for bearing analysis includes gathering operating data from monitoring devices, analyzing service and maintenance records and charts, securing application diagrams/graphics/engineering drawings, preparing an inspection sheet, and taking photographs throughout the procedure [EV-K01-005]. These are preparation and recording recommendations only; no operating records, drawings, photographs, lubricant identity, or samples have actually been collected in this demonstration, and the scenario's assumed cause (external vibration during standstill) is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference [EV-K01-005][EV-K01-006]. The cleaning-order card registers evidence-preservation order only and does not authorize the page's solvents or cleaning actions for an unknown machine, so an approved cleaning procedure for this unidentified equipment cannot be treated as already available [EV-K01-009].

Evidence limitations:
Evidence scope is registered generic bearing education only; no model-specific, aviation, or reuse authorization is provided.
No sample quantity, container model, product selection, or laboratory acceptance threshold is supplied in the cited steps [EV-K01-006].
The cleaning-order card does not authorize selecting cleaning agents or performing disassembly/cleaning for an unknown machine; an applicable approved procedure would be needed [EV-K01-009].
No actual device records, lubricant container identity/specification/batch, or collected samples/photographs are available in this demonstration [EV-K01-005][EV-K01-006].
The assumed cause of external vibration during standstill is a teaching assumption, not a source-proven fact or classifier inference.
The cited material does not establish actual damage cause, numerical maintenance parameters, or aircraft release.
Sources:
